clue.text: As desired he had got outside work

indicators.note: the contracted pronoun-verb pair has got around the outside of the job word, enclosing it

parts.note: he had contracts to he'd
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Things turned out as hoped once he had gone outdoors to do a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link: the definition is the past-tense verb 'desired', not 'As desired'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have wished for something is to have desired it; the two past-tense verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Leather sure to be inflexible

parts.note: a hide is an animal skin used as leather
bound, as in bound to happen, means sure

explanation.surface: Leather is guaranteed to stay stiff and unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone narrow and set in their ways, unable to change, is called hidebound.

clue.text: Father takes the French food and finds it pleasant to taste

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
la is a French word for 'the'
table means the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Dad tries a French dish and enjoys its flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just strings the pieces together; 'and finds it' is link material before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is agreeable on the tongue is palatable, a synonym for tasty.

clue.text: Drink prescribed by doctor before morning

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, morning

explanation.surface: A medic recommends a nip of whisky first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is the order indicator; 'prescribed by' is linking surface fitting the medical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small measure of spirits such as whisky, so a drink.

clue.text: Refused it anyway having had more than enough

indicators.note: taken as 'any way', the letters can be put together in any order

explanation.surface: Someone declined a dish anyway, being already stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' signals rearranging the nine letters of REFUSED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surfeited is to have been fed to excess, overfull.

clue.text: Delightful mood 'ad being of an amiable disposition

parts.note: sweet means charming or delightful
having a mood, Cockney 'ad for had, gives tempered, having a certain temper

explanation.surface: A Cockney speaker reports someone had a lovely mood, being good-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ad is dropped-aitch had: having a mood (temper) is being tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with an easy, kindly nature is described as sweet-tempered, or amiable.

clue.text: Be paid whilst learning

indicators.note: whilst says the answer sits during, and so within, the word that follows

explanation.surface: Get a wage while still in training, like an apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside lEARNing; 'whilst' marks it as contained in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive money for work done is to earn it.

clue.text: Agree unconditionally to leave

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so the word just before it departs from the adverb

parts.note: totally means completely, without conditions
taken as written

explanation.surface: Consent without reservations to departing.
explanation.walkthrough: TOTALLY (unconditionally) loses TO, as 'to leave' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally correspond or match, so they agree.

clue.text: It is silly to include Rex in the sketch

indicators.note: the foolish word takes in the royal letter, holding it inside

parts.note: daft means silly
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone says it is foolish to draw the king into a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, like a rough sketch.

clue.text: Girl wasn't well on the way back

indicators.note: travelling back means the past-tense verb is read from its end to its start

parts.note: ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A young woman felt unwell during the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: AILED backwards gives the name DELIA; the printed DELTA is a misprint of that I.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a woman's given name, so a girl.

clue.text: Emerald'sa possibility for the girl

indicators.note: a possibility is one of several arrangements, so these letters may be shuffled into another

explanation.surface: A gemstone suggests a name to give a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EMERALD'S A (the printed run lacks a space); those nine letters rearranged give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is a woman's name, famously the dancer in The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Attractive guide for lost travellers?

parts.note: a compass needle is drawn magnetically toward a point that helps wanderers find their way; attractive means pulling like a magnet

explanation.surface: A charming tour leader for people who have strayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass needle points to the magnetic pole, guiding travellers by its pull.

clue.text: City striker hard to follow

indicators.note: the hardness letter comes after, following the striking implement

parts.note: a bat is something used for striking a ball
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A city's centre forward is a tough act to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer but is a bat; 'to follow' puts H after BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England.

clue.text: Something to act upon

parts.note: read literally, a platform that actors perform on, not a matter to respond to

explanation.surface: A matter one should respond to.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre platform is where actors perform, literally what one acts on.

clue.text: Nothing yet developed on this small island

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: No building has yet taken place on this tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on this' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (or ait) is a small island in a river, such as in the Thames.

clue.text: Arguments are said to stir up

indicators.note: said signals that the arguments word is spoken and its sound matches the answer

parts.note: rows are quarrels, rhyming with cows

explanation.surface: Quarrels are reported to inflame passions.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWS (rhyming with 'cows') sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to awaken or provoke, to stir up feelings.

clue.text: Go in some pain

indicators.note: in places the travel verb within the quantity word

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Head over in a degree of discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is fodder taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme suffering, physical or mental.

clue.text: Fragmentary language of an overseas visitor perhaps

definitions.text: Fragmentary language of an overseas visitor perhaps

parts.words: Fragmentary language of an overseas visitor perhaps
parts.note: the faltering, imperfect speech of a foreigner learning the tongue, read literally as a shattered language

explanation.surface: A tourist speaks in halting phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperfect speech by a non-native speaker is called this, the tongue being metaphorically shattered.

clue.text: I will be deemed as being rash

parts.note: contracts to I'll
judged means considered or deemed

explanation.surface: A speaker fears being thought reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as being' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly thought-out, hasty decision is ill-judged, meaning imprudent.

clue.text: Passes the fish as a friendly gesture

parts.note: hands means passes, as in handing something over
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone hands over the seafood as a kind gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's palm is a greeting or sign of goodwill.

clue.text: What to wear at dinner and dance or nothing?

definitions.text: What to wear at dinner and dance or nothing?

parts.words: What to wear at dinner and dance or nothing?
parts.note: invitations may state that formal attire is not required; taken jokingly, guests could come in nothing at all

explanation.surface: A guest wonders about the evening's dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: An event where clothing is not compulsory, wryly offering nudity as a choice.

clue.text: Heartless boy holding a first born child

indicators.note: the shortened lad word holds the other letters inside it
heartless removes the central letter of the lad word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An uncaring lad is cradling a firstborn infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' turns BOY into BY, 'holding' puts A plus B (first of 'born') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is a very young child, an infant.

clue.text: Singer included one fundamental ingredient

indicators.note: the vocalist word took the numeral within it

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced male singer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vocalist brought in an essential element.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or chief constituent of something.

clue.text: Artist in container finds mineral

indicators.note: in places the painter abbreviation within the receptacle

parts.note: a box is a container
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter inside a crate discovers some rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Borax is a white mineral, sodium borate, used in cleaning products.

clue.text: Brought the present

parts.note: read grammatically, the present tense of the verb whose past is brought, not a gift being carried

explanation.surface: Someone carried a gift along.
explanation.definitionFit: The present-tense form of that verb, whose past form is 'brought'.

clue.text: Sheds thus out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: This way, the outbuildings are broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' could be a verb; here it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Huts are small simple buildings, like garden sheds.

clue.text: Model getting in the money at the festival

indicators.note: the car letter gets in among the payment letters

parts.note: a fee is money paid
T, as in the Ford Model T

explanation.surface: A fashion model is paid at the summer fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; it is the Model T Ford, giving T. 'the' and 'at the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or fair, often a village fundraiser.

clue.text: Image, potentially old one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A picture that may be an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD plus I (one) rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or statue worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Almost certain to give yield

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
render means give, as in render assistance

explanation.surface: Being nearly sure means giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its final E, 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or yield to an opponent.

clue.text: Follow mother's principle

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Keep to a parent's guiding rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has').
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a firmly held belief or tenet laid down as true.

clue.text: The last but four to score

definitions.text: The last but four to score

parts.words: The last but four to score
parts.note: a score is twenty, so counting up to it, this is the item four places before the final one

explanation.surface: Someone is the fifth-from-last to get a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' means twenty, not to get a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Of twenty ordinal positions, number sixteen is followed by four more.

clue.text: Shelf is not long enough for the book

indicators.note: falling short in length means the book word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a ledger is an account book

explanation.surface: The bookcase is too short for the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: LEDGER is cut short, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf projecting from a wall.
